name: St. Leonhard im Pitztal
kurzbeschreibung: Highest village in the Pitztal, with direct access to the Pitzaler Gletscher and Rifflsee.
beschreibung:
Überblick

St. Leonhard im Pitztal is situated in the upper Pitztal valley in the Tyrolean district of Imst at an elevation of 1,366 metres above sea level, spanning an impressive valley length of around 25 kilometres up to the high alpine head of the valley. Covering an area of more than 223 square kilometres, St. Leonhard is the largest municipality by area in the Imst district and the third largest in North Tyrol. The municipality encompasses more than 30 picturesque hamlets and settlements—including Scheibe, Mandarfen, Mittelberg, Neurur, Plangeross, and Zaunhof—nestled harmoniously between the Kaunergrat ridge to the west and the Geigenkamm to the east. The valley is crowned by the Wildspitze (3,768 m), the highest peak in North Tyrol. St. Leonhard delights mountaineers and winter sports enthusiasts with its pristine natural environment, the Pitztaler Gletscher ski area, and its status as the historic habitat of the largest Alpine ibex colony in the Eastern Alps.

Geschichte

Permanent settlement in the inner Pitztal valley began comparatively late during the High Middle Ages. The first dairy settlements (Schwaighöfe) of the Tyrolean sovereigns and the Lords of Starkenberg are documented from the 13th century; the traditional Schrofenhof estate was recorded as early as 1265, while the valley was referred to as 'im Puzzental' around the same time. Around 1300, the name of the patron saint Saint Leonhard appeared in records for the first time. Until 21 February 1935, the political municipality was officially named 'Pitzthal' before being renamed after the patron saint of its parish church. The baroque parish church of Saint Leonhard in Scheibe was constructed between 1761 and 1762 replacing a late Gothic chapel, featuring exquisite Rococo frescoes. A pioneering European conservation feat was achieved in 1953: on the steep slopes of Schrofenhof, a reintroduction project was launched for the Alpine ibex, which had previously been exterminated in the Eastern Alps. With the opening of the Pitz-Express funicular railway in 1983 and the construction of the Wildspitzbahn in 2012, the village evolved into one of the premier glacier destinations in the Alps.

Anreise

By car, St. Leonhard is accessible via the Inntal motorway A12 taking the Imst/Pitztal exit. From there, follow the Pitztal Landesstraße (L16) up the valley, passing Wenns and Jerzens to reach the village centre of St. Leonhard after roughly 25 kilometres and the valley head at Mittelberg and Mandarfen after 37 kilometres. Train passengers travel along the Arlberg railway line (ÖBB Railjet and WESTbahn) to Imst-Pitztal railway station. Directly outside the station, VVT regional bus route 4204 connects all settlements along the valley at frequent intervals. Holidaymakers enjoy complimentary travel on the valley buses using the Pitztal guest card.

Tipps

An essential highlight is taking the state-of-the-art Wildspitzbahn cable car up to the Hinterer Brunnenkogel (3,440 m) within the Pitztaler Gletscher ski domain: the futuristic Café 3.440 located at the summit is Austria's highest coffee house and registry office, featuring a cantilevered viewing terrace with panoramic views of more than fifty three-thousand-metre peaks. In summer, take the Rifflseebahn lift to lake Rifflsee (2,232 m), the largest mountain lake in the Ötztal Alps, where Europe's highest raft excursion operates. Nature and culture enthusiasts should visit the Tiroler Steinbockzentrum at the historic Schrofenhof, offering interactive exhibitions, accessible panorama trails, and a spacious wildlife enclosure housing ibexes and marmots.
